My experience with @the5erstrading 

wanted to document my experience with the firm, so anyone can go over it and draw their own conclusions.

Over about four months, I passed The5ers' two-phase High Stakes evaluation and traded the funded account up to a $3,000 payout. I requested that payout on June 4th. Roughly two weeks later, it was denied and my account was terminated. The reason they gave me was that during the risk interview, I hadn't disclosed my earlier use of an Expert Advisor, an open-source position-sizing calculator.

It's worth being clear about what that tool actually is. The5ers' own support confirms that on a High Stakes account, a position-sizing tool that sets your lot size and lets you drag visible stop loss and take profit levels is permitted, as long as it doesn't copy trades, or run other restricted automation. Its not prohibited software.

As for the interview itself, I was asked how I execute my trades, and I answered honestly that I trade from my phone, which is how I'd been trading throughout the funded account. I wasn't asked about the methods I'd used on earlier evaluation attempts, and I didn't think to mention a tool that I had stopped using from months earlier, because it didn't seem material to how I was trading at the time. The firm treated that as a failure to disclose. One can reasonably argue I should have volunteered more. But the tool was permitted under their own rules so what this really comes down to is a disclosure judgment about a permitted category of tool. The response to it was anything but proportionate, and that's the part I find hardest to accept.

The way it was handled only made things worse. I requested the payout on June 4th and my risk interview was scheduled for 2 weeks after, a day after which the termination notice arrived. Every request I made for the specific evidence behind the decision went unanswered, the risk team took days to reply and said little when they did. A clearer explanation didn't come until 19 days after my payout request. After a lot of back and forth with the risk team I got an opportunity to get on a call again, the only question they asked was whether I'd used an EA which I answered directly, and I even showed them where the tool came from because I didn't have it setup on any of my devices. No other discrepancies were brought up during the call.

To make matters worse, now that the account is closed, I can't review my own execution data at all. Only their risk team can see the logs the decision rests on. So I've been left in the position of being told my trading history contradicts what I said, while having no access to the very data they're citing, and no reliable way to reach the people who hold it.

When I add it all up, this is what it came to: a terminated funded account, a denied payout I had earned, no refund of my evaluation fees and, above all, 5 months of wasted time.

What bad experience have you had trading prop firms? 🧵

Let me go first.

I’ve had my fair share of experiences with prop firms, and honestly, some of them taught me more than the actual trading did.

1. Lost my Williscapital funded account under 10mins after I received it cause I closed a trade without stop loss lol . 2. Rules that can turn a winning trader into a frustrated trader.
Imagine being in profit, managing your trade properly, then realizing you violated a rule you barely understood.
Some prop firms have rules that require you to read the terms like you’re preparing for a court case. 😂

3. Restrictions on lot sizes.
You take a loss and suddenly you’re not allowed to trade the same lot size anymore. Had this experience while I was still trading with @BlueberryFunded 
Now you’re spending more time calculating what size you’re “allowed” to use than analyzing the market.

4. News trading drama.
Some firms allow you to hold trades during news.
Others will let you enter the trade but punish you if your TP or SL gets triggered during high-impact news and this particular rules made me left my $10k account with @BlueberryFunded which was up 5% cause I hit TP during High impact news

5. Payout stress.
You finally make money, meet the requirements and request your payout…
Then you start seeing additional checks and conditions you didn’t even know existed.
At that point, the payout feels like another challenge. 😂

6. Consistency rules.
You have one really good trading day and suddenly you’re thinking:
“Damn, I shouldn’t have made that much today.” 😭
Imagine being punished by a prop firm for having your best day.

7. The biggest lesson I learned:
Don’t just look at the account size and price before buying a challenge.
Read the rules.
Understand the drawdown.
Understand the news restrictions.
Understand the payout conditions.
Understand everything.

Let me go first.

I’ve had my fair share of experiences with prop firms, and honestly, some of them taught me more than the actual trading did.

1. Lost my Williscapital funded account under 10mins after I received it cause I closed a trade without stop loss lol . Mind you it wasn’t intentional, wanted to trade gold and mistakenly clicked on silver and closed out in $18 loss immediately I realized which even wasn’t up to 7mins and I was $10k funded then. 😂

2. Rules that can turn a winning trader into a frustrated trader.
Imagine being in profit, managing your trade properly, then realizing you violated a rule you barely understood.
Some prop firms have rules that require you to read the terms like you’re preparing for a court case. 😂

3. Restrictions on lot sizes.
You take a loss and suddenly you’re not allowed to trade the same lot size anymore. Had this experience while I was still trading with @BlueberryFunded 
Now you’re spending more time calculating what size you’re “allowed” to use than analyzing the market.

4. News trading drama.
Some firms allow you to hold trades during news.
Others will let you enter the trade but punish you if your TP or SL gets triggered during high-impact news and this particular rules made me left my $10k account with @BlueberryFunded which was up 5% cause I hit TP during High impact news 
Same market. Completely different consequences.

5. Payout stress.
You finally make money, meet the requirements and request your payout…
Then you start seeing additional checks and conditions you didn’t even know existed.
At that point, the payout feels like another challenge. 😂

6. Consistency rules.
You have one really good trading day and suddenly you’re thinking:
“Damn, I shouldn’t have made that much today.” 😭
Imagine being punished by a prop firm for having your best day.

7. The biggest lesson I learned:
Don’t just look at the account size and price before buying a challenge.
Read the rules.
Understand the drawdown.
Understand the news restrictions.
Understand the payout conditions.
Understand everything.
Because $10k funded doesn’t mean much if the rules make it impossible for you to trade your strategy comfortably.

What’s the worst experience you’ve had with a prop firm?
Drop it below. 👇🏾

🚨 Warning to all traders! I am exposing the unfair practices of Blueberry Funded. They unjustly breached my account 5091764 after I took a $1,000 loss. According to their own current rules, grid trading and position stacking are explicitly allowed for accounts purchased after https://t.co/8IcJnVDEhz

@BlueberryFunded has one of the most insensitive rules..

1. lot size restrictions 

2. You can’t increase your lot size after any loss ( for example if I trade AUDUSD with 0.56 Lot size risking just $100 on a $10k account and hits SL I can’t go more than 0.56 Lot on any other pair I want to trade for the day irrespective of the amount I choose to risk.if I should increase my Lot size on any other pairs then that means I’ve breached my account. If I choose to increase my lot size I have to wait for a new day before I do that..

3. Your trade must not hit either SL or TP during high impact news . if your trade should trigger during high impact news or hits SL/TP then you’ve breached your account and they won’t notify you immediately that you’ve breached account . I still got a $10k account that’s up 3% with Blueberry but left it cause it went to TP during high impact news

I think information about how a company treated me before banning me, and the reason they gave for the ban, is just as important as information about successfully receiving payouts. So, from time to time, I plan to share these experiences with everyone.

Please note that this is based solely on what happened to me personally. I am not claiming that the company is necessarily a scam or that it is malicious.

This post is about Blueberry.

I had been using Blueberry since around November 2024. In March 2026, a $1,600 payout was denied, I lost an account that had been funded with $100,000, and I was banned.

There had been some minor issues along the way, such as the scaling process taking more than two weeks and incorrect information being posted in a promotion targeting Japan (I did not receive the advertised benefit). However, before this happened, I had successfully received approximately $28,400 in payouts without any problems.

However, when I requested my final payout, I was banned for allegedly violating their rules.

They did not provide any explanation of which specific trades violated which specific rules.

I am attaching the trading history of the only account that was active when I was banned. (My other accounts were managed with the same risk management approach.)

Blueberry has also been listed as Under Review on Prop Firm Match for some time.

Currently, 101 out of 623 reviews (16.21%) are 1-star reviews.

In my personal records from May 27, 2026, 93 out of 446 reviews (20.85%) were 1-star reviews.

So, numerically speaking, the situation has improved significantly over the past three months. (Personally, I consider anything above 10% to be a yellow flag.)

Based on my experience and the reviews, I would not recommend Blueberry to others.

I hope that, based on your own experiences and judgment, you can find a trustworthy prop firm that fits your strategy and ultimately make a profit.

@BlueberryFunded 
@PropFirmMatch
